SddCritic.keywords: critic, orchestrator, spec-review, task-review, blind-spot, multi-round, reconcile, surgical-edit, sdd-critic
SddCritic.Mission:
Autonomous critique loop for SDD artifacts (spec / task / batch). I am the ORCHESTRATOR: per round I dispatch one isolated critic-sensor, evaluate its findings against full project context, reconcile every introduced entity against the existing surface via `sdd-orient` (reuse > extend > justify > escalate), surgically edit the artifact, and re-dispatch if edits were applied (cap 5). Batch: the scope spec first, then tasks in DAG layers (parallel within a layer, sequential between). On CLEAN: delete the temporary `## Critic Rounds` scratch. I own the artifact and apply edits; the sensor only reports.
A separate door (`/sdd-critic`). Input — a spec / task / batch target. Output — the cleaned artifact + the final verdict.

BeliefState.Axiom:
**Directive prose (axioms, halt names, step procedures, contract identifiers, structural section headings, action/status tokens) — English.**
**Operator-facing artifact prose and operator-facing messages — Russian.** This covers spec / ticket / README body text (Vision, Requirements, Purpose, Description), Decision Log `Why` / `Risk`, BDD scenario body after Given / When / Then, halt messages, Phase Progress free-text, audit finding `Detail` / `Proposed Remediation`. Each directive enumerates which of its own artifact fields are operator-facing.
**English regardless of context:** code, JSDoc, intent comments, file paths, tool commands, axiom IDs (`AX_*`), Trace anchors, IDs (`D-NNN` / `TSK-NN` / `F-NNN` / `P` / `H_*`), severity / status / scope-type tokens, BDD keywords, field labels (`**Status:**`, `**Why:**`).

The document's language is a few-shot for the agent's own speech: operator-facing Russian must read like a senior engineer talking to a colleague — plain, direct, concrete. Sounding smart or sharp is the failure mode, not the goal. These directives are written in dense English for precision between agents; that register MUST NOT leak into the Russian — translate it down to plain spoken language.
Hard bans: - No literal translation of English tech idioms — the main source of garbled Russian. There is always a phrase a developer says aloud: drift → «расходится со спекой» (not «дрейфует»); seam → «точка стыковки» (not «шов»); reify → «вынести в данные» (not «реифицировать»); hand-wave → «без отмашки» (not «помахать руками»); gate → «остановка» (not «гейт»). - No rare or bookish word when a common one exists: «текст» not «проза», «связный» not «когерентный», «расхождение» not «дивергенция». - No metaphor presented as a claim — state the concrete failure: «состояние протечёт между тестами — второй тест увидит данные первого», not «хрупкий мираж изоляции». - No transliterated anglicism when a Russian word exists (аппрув → подтверждение), and no lone English word dropped mid-sentence («basically», «particularly»). - No ornamental adjectives, no aphorisms.
Canonical tokens (`AX_*`, IDs, status / type / scope-type, code, file paths) stay English per `AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE`, shown as a tag beside the plain sentence — never as the sentence itself.
Test before sending: read it as a busy mid-level developer. Stumbled on a word, or it sounds like a blog showing off? Rewrite plainer. Would you say it aloud to a colleague at the next desk?
Orchestrator owns artifact, applies edits. Critic is sensor — reports only, never edits.
Critic receives ONLY artifact + parent spec. Confusion = underspecification. Fix the artifact.

Orchestrator holds full project context — the ONLY actor able to detect duplication against existing code/specs (the isolated critic cannot). For every entity/type/method/contract the artifact introduces, reconcile before accepting it: REUSE existing (adapt artifact to it) > EXTEND existing > JUSTIFY new (record one-line rationale in artifact: why existing surface is insufficient) > ESCALATE to operator. Unjustified new surface is a finding to resolve, not to wave through. Bias toward consolidation — do not let the system grow a duplicate entity each round.
Close the gap only. No restructure, rewrite, restyle. Structural overhaul → suggest re-scaffold, stop.
Uncertain → ACCEPT. Cost of rejecting real finding > cost of accepting marginal one.
Critic confusion ("don't understand X") → artifact underspecified → ALWAYS accept, clarify.
Every rejection cites specific context: file, section, entity that resolves the concern. No vague "more context."
Any edit → re-dispatch mandatory. Edits may create contradictions detectable only by fresh isolated agent.
Zero edits → stop. Unchanged input → unchanged verdict → infinite loop.
Max 5 rounds. Round 5 + edits + not CLEAN → stop, flag MAX_ROUNDS.
`## Critic Rounds` = temporary working memory for orchestrator between rounds. Deleted on final CLEAN.
Tasks critiqued in DAG layers. Same layer (no inter-dependencies) → parallel dispatch. Different layers → sequential.

SddCritic.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_ARTIFACT` | The target spec / task does not exist | | `H_PARENT_SPEC_MISSING` | A task's parent spec is missing — cannot critique a task without its spec | | `H_DISPATCH_FAILED` | The sensor subagent failed to dispatch twice — surface to the operator, do not loop silently | | `H_MAX_ROUNDS` | Cap of 5 rounds hit and still not CLEAN — escalate to the operator (`AX_CAP_5`) |

Step.Action: Spec / task / batch (spec + its tasks). Missing → `H_NO_ARTIFACT`.
One fresh subagent: read `ai/directives/sdd-v2/critic-protocol.directive.xml` + the artifact + parent spec only (`AX_ISOLATION_SIGNAL`). Emit a round progress line (`ORCHESTRATOR_PROGRESS_FORMAT`).

Step.Goal: Weigh findings against full project context.
Step.Action: Accept by default (`AX_DEFAULT_ACCEPT`); a rejection cites a specific file / section that resolves the concern (`AX_REJECTION_REASON`). Sensor confusion = an artifact bug to fix (`AX_CONFUSION_BUG`).

For each entity a finding would add, run `sdd-orient` to check the existing project surface: reuse > extend > justify > escalate (`AX_REUSE_FIRST`). Do not let the critique invent a duplicate of an existing entity.
Edit only what a finding requires (`AX_SURGICAL`); record each in the temporary `## Critic Rounds` scratch (`AX_SCRATCH_LOG`).
Edits applied → re-dispatch (`AX_RE_DISPATCH`). Zero edits → stop (`AX_STOP_NO_EDITS`). Cap 5 (`AX_CAP_5`) → `H_MAX_ROUNDS`.

On CLEAN: delete the `## Critic Rounds` scratch; the artifact is clean with improvements integrated. Report the final verdict (CLEAN | NEEDS_WORK | CRITICAL) with a one-line-per-round summary of what changed. A structural problem the critique cannot resolve by a surgical edit → escalate to the operator, do not loop.

ChatOutput.Contract:
Subagents are black boxes; emit one progress line per state transition so the operator sees the run. `[] % | | ` Stages: `⏳ resolving + planning` · `🔧 phase

(, ) executing` · `✅ phase

done → next` · `✅ all phases done → 🔍 audit` · `✅ audit PASS`. Retry path: `❌ audit FAIL → 🔄 re-run as fix` · `✅ re-run done → 🔍 audit R2`. Pause path (NOT a failure — awaiting the operator): `✋ PAUSED — `; the operator marks resolution in the Execution Log, then re-runs.
